method: tools/parity/oidc-differential.cjs against isolated copies of the API-initialized fixture, with one ephemeral local RS256 provider
normalization: Random UUIDs, access/refresh tokens, ID tokens, and timestamps are not retained; compare their semantic effects via selected user fields, redirect shape, and session count.
Node and Go use separate copied fixture directories and database files.

JSON object member order is canonicalized for Socket.IO event payload comparison because JSON object order is not semantically significant; array order, scalar values, null versus empty, and the linked user's raw persisted extraData text remain strict.
limits: Covered web auto-registration success, provider error, replay after provider error, expired ID-token rejection, existing-user email linking, disabled auto-registration denial, and one real-socket user_added recipient/payload case.
Did not exercise invalid signature/issuer/audience/nonce, mobile flow, expiry of in-memory flow state, callback cookies in detail, or the general Socket.IO event inventory.
The report establishes only these six local mock-provider cases, not overall OIDC or identity parity.
